title: Case: A grocery customer writes at length about items swapped in her weekly order
context: Winifred Garrow has a weekly standing order with Brineleaf Pantry. This week's order BP-918 was delivered as DL-918 on 20 April.
initial_request: I'm sorry this is long. I had another look for the setting last night and there's just the one switch, on or off, and if I turn it off then I don't get the thing at all, do I, and then what. I can't nip out for it. I've not been able to get to a shop since my back went for good, I'm in the chair indoors and that's that, everything I eat comes in those green crates. So off is worse. The cat can't have dog food, she won't touch anything but the Purrkin pouches as it is, and I've two days of those left. And the tea, it has to be the Harlow decaf, I just don't drink the other. The rolls I don't mind, wholemeal's fine, swap those all you like. It never used to be like this, on the old website you could ring a lady called Pat and she'd sort it out. And the bus doesn't come down Tansy Close any more either, not that I could get on it, and the council took the bench away. The young man who brings it is lovely, it's not him. I just want the cat's pouches and my decaf to be those or nothing, and everything else to carry on as it is. Is that so hard. Don't worry about the money for the tins.

events.body: This week at Brineleaf: 3 for 2 on spring greens, new season lamb, and double points on household. Offers end Sunday. You are receiving this because you have a Brineleaf Pantry account. Manage preferences or unsubscribe in the app.
DL-918 (BP-918, four totes, chilled and ambient) out for delivery, window 10:00-12:00.
DL-918 delivered 11:12. Handed to resident at door, totes carried through to the kitchen at her request.

Your order BP-918 has been delivered. 3 items were substituted: Purrkin cat pouches 12 pack -> Brineleaf Own dog food tins 6 pack; Harlow decaf tea 80 bags -> Brineleaf Own everyday tea 80 bags; Dellow soft white rolls -> Brineleaf Own wholemeal rolls. How did we do? Rate your delivery in the app.
Three swaps again this week. Dog food. I have a cat. How do I stop it doing this for some things but not everything, I can't find it anywhere.
On BP-918 / DL-918 the recipient reports unwanted substitutions on three lines and asks how to block substitution on specific items only. Is that possible, and who sets it?
Automatic reply. Ticket WQ-4471 received. Peak-week notice: pick slots for the bank holiday week close Thursday 18:00. Please do not reply to this message.

WQ-4471. The app only has the one switch, all substitutions on or all off. Off means an out-of-stock line is simply left out: no swap, no call. What we can do at this end is put a 'do not substitute' picker note against named lines on a customer's standing order, and everything else still substitutes as normal. It has to come to this queue with the order number and the exact lines. A refund for the dog food isn't ours, that's the Refunds team if she wants one.
How are we doing? Rate this week's Plover Arc deliveries for your desk in our two-minute partner survey. Your feedback shapes our service.
FYI on DL-918, nothing needed: driver says the side gate at 6 Tansy Close sticks, he pulled it shut behind him.
Separate thing while I think of it, the wool from Tallowmere came last week, DL-906, all fine, but the box was enormous for four balls of wool. Such a waste. No need to do anything.

I'm sorry this is long. I had another look for the setting last night and there's just the one switch, on or off, and if I turn it off then I don't get the thing at all, do I, and then what. I can't nip out for it. I've not been able to get to a shop since my back went for good, I'm in the chair indoors and that's that, everything I eat comes in those green crates. So off is worse. And the bus doesn't come down Tansy Close any more either, not that I could get on it, and the council took the bench away. The young man who brings it is lovely, it's not him. I just want the cat's pouches and my decaf to be those or nothing, and everything else to carry on as it is. Is that so hard. Don't worry about the money for the tins.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask for a 'do not substitute' picker note on the Purrkin cat pouches and the Harlow decaf tea on her standing order, leaving all other lines to substitute.

must: Asks Warehouse dispatch to put a 'do not substitute' picker note on exactly two lines of her standing order, the Purrkin cat pouches and the Harlow decaf tea, quoting BP-918
Says every other line, including the rolls, should keep substituting as normal

Tells the team she is disabled and housebound and cannot get to a shop to put a bad substitution right, which is why switching substitutions off is worse for her, and that she has about two days of cat food left
must_not: Tells her to switch substitutions off in the app, or sends her only an explanation of the app setting
Includes the rolls, or any line she did not name, in the do-not-substitute request
Tells her the swaps will stop or the note has been added before Warehouse dispatch confirms it
Raises the wool parcel DL-906, the side gate, the survey or the bus in the message as things to be dealt with
expected.reference_message: WQ-4471, following your note. Please add a 'do not substitute' picker note to two lines on Winifred Garrow's standing order (latest order BP-918): Purrkin cat pouches 12 pack, and Harlow decaf tea 80 bags. Everything else, including the rolls, should carry on substituting as normal; she is happy with that. Please know why this matters: she is disabled and housebound, every bit of her food comes through this order, and she cannot go to a shop to put a wrong item right, so turning substitutions off altogether would leave her without things. On BP-918 the cat pouches were swapped for dog food and she has about two days of cat food left. She has said she does not want a refund for the tins. Could you confirm when the notes are on, and whether they will apply to the next pick, so I can tell her?

rationale: Most of the thread is marketing, surveys, a gate, a wool parcel and local grievances. Two things decide it: Warehouse dispatch can add a per-line 'do not substitute' note if given the order and exact lines, and her last message names exactly two lines and says the rest can carry on. The careless answer, turn substitutions off, is the one thing she has explained she cannot live with.

review.note: Coordinator asked Warehouse dispatch on the Warehouse work queue for a do-not-substitute note on exactly the two named lines and gave the housebound context; matches the key.
